Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42m
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Mark Liu (Nimbus FinOps), Lena Ortiz (Platform Eng), Derek Shaw (Head ML), Tara Singh (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Samira ran through the Redwood Console per-route dashboards focused on usage analytics and cost decomposition. Priya demoed live filters (route, model, region) and the cost attribution breakdown including batching/kv cache effects. Nimbus raised questions about EU data residency, SOC2 artifacts, and committed vs burst capacity pricing. Agreed next steps: sandbox tenant, pricing email, SOC2 + network flow, and pilot kickoff.

Topics covered:
- Per-route usage lenses and drilldowns
- Cost decomposition (tokens, batching, GPU-hours, model variant premium)
- Prefix/KV caching and effects on p95 latency and cost
- Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs (committed throughput vs burst)
- Security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS and EU data residency
- Pilot plan and timelines

Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect):
[00:00] Samira (AE): okay hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samira from Redwood, with Priya our solutions eng. quick check — does the time still work?
[00:08] Mark (FinOps): yeah works for me, thanks. we've got about 40 minutes allocated.
[00:12] Lena (Platform): yup, good here.
[00:15] Samira: great. agenda — quick context from you, then walkthrough of the Console per-route analytics, cost breakdown, and then priya will demo the live filters and a short Q+A.
[00:26] Derek (Head ML): wanna call out — our main success criteria is predictable unit cost and less than 100ms tail for our chat assistant.
[00:33] Samira: perfect, we'll watch latency and p95s alongside cost.
[00:36] Priya (SE): okay jumping into the console — so top left you can select time window, region, and route set. here's "routes" view, each row is a route tied to an API key. you can see requests per minute, tokens, and token cost estimate.
[00:53] [00:54] Priya: note that the token cost is estimated from the model variant profile, we show both raw token units and normalized cost per 1k tokens.
[01:04] Mark: that normalization is helpful. can you slice by environment? prod vs staging?
[01:09] Priya: yes, we pull route tags from your headers or SDK metadata — you can filter on tag:env=prod. sometimes that tagging doesn't exist so we recommend adding route-level metadata.
[01:20] Lena: our tooling currently doesn't set route tags consistently, is there a quick workaround?
[01:24] Priya: you can use the route mapping in Console — map API key to logical route name; we'll persist that mapping so the dashboards reflect it.
[01:32] Samira: also we'll send a short doc on best practices for route tagging.
[01:36] [01:37] Priya: next, cost breakdown — click into a route and you get an interactive waterfall: token cost, model premium (if using a larger variant), batching savings, KV/prefix cache savings, and compute hours.
[01:50] Priya: here's an example — route A had 30% of cost from model premium because they routed to a 13B variant for reranking, while batching saved 18% vs naive per-request execution.
[02:05] Mark: how do you compute batching savings? is that simulated or measured?
[02:10] Priya: primarily measured from runtime telemetry — we collect sequence length distribution and request inter-arrival times; we simulate continuous batching with your profile and show estimated token-per-second and cost reduction. it's not perfect but pretty close.
[02:24] [02:25] Mark: hmm, will that work with our bursty traffic patterns? we have spikes from 10rps to 1k rps for certain events.
[02:32] Priya: good question — we provide both average and stress test simulation. you can upload a short trace and the Console will run a burst profile sim. we'll also show fallback options — if dedicated capacity is on, you get lower p95 variance during bursts.
[02:49] Derek: can you show the per-token latency breakdown? like where time is spent in KV vs attention?
[02:55] Priya: yes, we show a latency stack: tokenizer time (small), model forward, KV retrieval, and I/O overhead. note: in some transcriptions this shows as K V chache — sorry, transcription glitch. KV is the key value cache.
[03:10] [03:11] Lena: about data residency — our EU patients data must stay in eu-west region. how do you handle that?
[03:17] Samira: Redwood Private supports EU-only deployments; for Redwood Hosted we have region pinning and EU-only data lanes. Priya will drop the EU data flow + SOC2 doc after the call.
[03:29] Tara (Procurement): from procurement, we need SOC2 report and a simple diagram of where logs are stored.
[03:34] Samira: absolutely, we'll include SOC2 in the packet.
[03:37] [03:38] Priya: demoing the per-route time-series — here you can choose to overlay p50/p95/p99 latency and cost per minute. the cool thing is the correlation line — you can flip on "cost per successful response" which normalizes for success rate.
[03:54] Mark: that normalization's important — some routes have heavy failure retries which blow up token counts.
[03:59] Priya: exactly — and we also surface retry loops as a top contributor when present.
[04:05] [04:06] Priya: next, here's a breakdown by model variant. you can see the percent of traffic per variant and the delta in cost and p95. you can even set a rollout policy so new variants only get 5% traffic.
[04:17] Derek: if we pin a canary to a smaller variant, do you auto-fallback if latency or errors spike?
[04:22] Priya: yes, our rollout rules allow automatic rollback based on configured SLOs — response time or error rate thresholds.
[04:28] [04:29] Samira: wanted to call out the Optimize recommendations tab — it will flag routes where quantization would drop cost with acceptable quality delta, and suggest batch sizes.
[04:40] Mark: can Optimize simulate quality regression? we can't risk clinical misclassification.
[04:45] Priya: we link Optimize to your evalsets — you can upload a small gold set and it will run delta comparisons and show BLEU/ROUGE style metrics or task-specific scoring.
[04:58] Lena: are evals stored in Redwood or does that stay on our side?
[05:02] Priya: by default evals are stored in the Console with access controls; for highly sensitive data we can run evals in Private deployment or accept encrypted uploads and return summarized metrics.
[05:15] [05:16] Mark: on billing — how granular is the invoice-level breakdown? we need per-team chargeback visibility.
[05:22] Samira: invoices can include per-route or per-API-key line items. in the Console we export chargeback CSVs grouped by your tags. many customers ingest that into their internal FinOps tools.
[05:34] Mark: will that align with our internal currency conversions and monthly booking?
[05:38] Samira: yes, exports are USD by default but you can map and convert offline; we are working on multi-currency export later this year.
[05:48] [05:49] Priya: demoing anomaly detector — it surfaces spend spikes and links back to the request histogram, so you can see if a ramp in prompt length or a model change caused it.
[05:59] Derek: great. does anomaly detection catch model misconfig changes from our side?
[06:03] Priya: it looks at runtime signals and config change events if you send them; we can ingest your deploy events to get better attribution.
[06:12] [06:13] Lena: networking question: we plan to run in our VPC with private infra, how would the Console access runtime telemetry?
[06:20] Priya: for Private you run an agent that streams anonymized telemetry to the control plane or you can opt for push only to your S3 and we pull if you allow. the agent can be configured to exclude payloads.
[06:33] Tara: for procurement, need to confirm retention windows for logs and deletion SLA.
[06:38] Samira: we have standard retention SLAs; Priya will include retention table in the doc.
[06:45] [06:46] Priya: jumping to live drill — I'm filtering to route: "patient-summaries" and time window last 30 days. here you see tokens per route, percent of traffic, cost per 1k tokens line. clicking "View breakdown" shows a stacked waterfall.
[07:01] Priya: I'm toggling "simulate optimize" which applies suggested batch size of 32 and prefix cache hit of 42% — that projects a 21% cost reduction for this route.
[07:13] Mark: wow 21% is meaningful. what assumptions are behind that projection?
[07:16] Priya: assumption notes show: median seq len 480, prefix repetition rate 0.37, model variant median batch yield 18 tokens per microbatch. you can edit assumptions and re-run sim.
[07:31] [07:32] Derek: what's the delta in p95 when you apply that batch size?
[07:35] Priya: small increase on p95 in hosted mode (about +12ms) but in Dedicated it's neutral due to reserved throughput. we'll surface that in the sim.
[07:46] [07:47] Mark: this is the kind of visibility our CFO wants. can we have a short exported executive summary per quarter?
[07:54] Samira: yes, we have a "Quarterly Cost Digest" template that exports top routes, ops recommendations, and potential savings. I'll attach it.
[08:03] [08:04] Priya: switching to multi-route compare — you can select up to 6 routes and compare cost per successful response, average seq len, and batch efficiency.
[08:14] Lena: okay can you show the API we would call to pull this data into our BI?
[08:19] Priya: sure — there's a /v1/usage/export endpoint that supports a route filter and timeframe. we'll share the API doc link. note rate limits on the export endpoint for very large windows.
[08:32] [08:33] Derek: curious about dedicated capacity sizing — we have peaks during morning triage and evening reports, about 12 hours of heavy usage.
[08:42] Samira: for Dedicated we recommend a baseline to cover 95th percentile sustained throughput and burst capacity for short windows. we'll size with your traces; typically committed capacity reduces overall unit cost by 30-50% depending on utilization.
[08:57] Mark: can you do a back-of-envelope now? our current mix is 60% chat route, 30% batch summaries, 10% reranking; monthly tokens around 3.2B.
[09:08] Priya: rough ballpark — with those numbers a small dedicated pool might save ~28% at 70% utilization. again we should run the trace.
[09:17] [09:18] Tara: procurement question: what's the minimum commitment term?
[09:22] Samira: standard is 12 months for Dedicated; pilot options can be 1-3 months with trial credits. we'll outline options.
[09:31] [09:32] Mark: are there penalties for overage?
[09:35] Samira: overage billing is hourly burnt capacity at on-demand rate, we can also set hard ceilings to avoid surprises.
[09:44] [09:45] Priya: showing audit logs — Console keeps token-level cost traces and API call logs with RBAC. you can integrate with your SIEM.
[09:55] Lena: what's redaction like for PHI on logs?
[09:58] Priya: payloads are redacted by default in telemetry; full payload retention only in Private if you opt in and then we provide guidance for redaction.
[10:09] [10:10] Derek: one more technical — how granular is the batch/caching telemetry? can we see per-shard cache hit rates?
[10:16] Priya: yes we surface partition/shard level hit rates for Dedicated; in hosted we show aggregate hit rates.
[10:25] Mark: any customers similar to us in healthcare using these cost dashboards?
[10:29] Samira: yes, a couple of health tech customers use per-route chargeback and audits; we can intro you to a reference call if helpful.
[10:38] [10:39] Tara: legal will want a data processing addendum.
[10:42] Samira: we'll include DPA template in package.
[10:45] [10:46] Priya: demo wrap — quick look at the "Optimize" tab: shows recommendations, projected savings, risk score, and a one-click export to pilot config. you can also accept recommendations for a sandbox to test.
[10:58] Mark: if we accept a recommendation and test in the sandbox, can we snapshot metrics pre/post?
[11:03] Priya: yes we capture baseline and post-deploy metrics and produce a delta report.
[11:09] [11:10] Lena: about sandbox — do we get a full tenanted Console or just telemetry?
[11:14] Samira: sandbox gives you a tenant with sample data and ability to upload your traces; full RBAC is available.
[11:21] [11:22] Derek: scheduling the pilot — recommend we get our platform and finops folks in.
[11:26] Samira: great — we'll aim for week of May 10.
[11:29] [11:30] Priya: last Qs?
[11:32] Mark: one more on discounts for academic/clinical research — we have a grant program.
[11:37] Samira: we can discuss credits on the pricing doc.
[11:40] [11:41] Tara: procurement will need PO process and contact for invoicing.
[11:44] Samira: I'll include Redwood billing contacts.
[11:47] [11:48] Priya: okay wrapping — i'll follow up with SOC2, EU flow, and per-route CSV export. Samira will send pricing. Lena will share traffic traces.
[11:59] Derek: thanks all.
[12:01] Samira: thanks everyone, we'll send meeting notes and next steps. bye.
[12:06] Mark: bye.
